name: Rumelian Turkish
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.verdict: a source was named but could not be reached
earlier_scan.source_named: Nemeth, Gyula 1965. Die Tuerken von Vidin: Sprache, Folklore, Religion (full description of a Rumelian Turkish variety incl. phonology); also Manevic 1953-54 (Glottolog ref)
earlier_scan.note: Print-only Rumelian Turkish dialect descriptions exist; none accessible online to verify a stress statement

sources.citation: Kappler, Matthias. 2023. Balkan Turkish dialect classifications. Dialectologia, special issue DIACLEU 2: 269-291. doi:10.1344/dialectologia2023.2023.10
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Survey of classifications (Németh, Hazai, Dryga, etc.); the only stress mention is Table 4, parameter 7 'Stress/pitch movement' in Dryga (2009)'s 20 parameters. No statement of where stress falls.

sources.citation: Katona, Louis K. 1969. Le dialecte turc de la Macédoine de l'Ouest. Türk Dili Araştırmaları Yıllığı - Belleten 17: 57-194.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Image-only scan; scanned 48 of 138 pages. Introduction (pp. 57-60), transcription key (pp. 61-62: vowel/consonant symbols, quality diacritics only), then riddles, songs and tales with French translation. No accent/stress statement in the scanned part; the remaining pages are texts/glossary. Source: https://dergipark.org.tr/tr/pub/belleten/article/443718.

sources.citation: Kakuk, Zsuzsanna. 1961. Die türkische Mundart von Küstendil und Michailovgrad. Acta Linguistica Academiae Scientiarum Hungaricae 11: 301-386.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Lautlehre §§1-19 (vowels, consonants, assimilation, geminates) then morphology/syntax §§20-34 and texts; no Betonung/Akzent section, no stress statement. Source: https://real-j.mtak.hu/814/.

sources.citation: Friedman, Victor A. 1982. Balkanology and Turcology: West Rumelian Turkish in Yugoslavia as reflected in prescriptive grammar. Studies in Slavic and General Linguistics 2: 1-77.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Image-only scan, scanned in full (41 PDF pages). Treats WRT phonological features (ö/ü > o/u, i > ı, ğ, harmony loss, etc.) and morphosyntax; no occurrence of stress/accent/penult in the scanned text. Silent. Source: https://home.uchicago.edu/~vfriedm/Articles/027Friedman82.pdf.

sources.citation: Kakuk, Suzanne. 1972. Le dialecte turc d'Ohrid en Macédoine. Acta Orientalia Academiae Scientiarum Hungaricae 26: 227-282.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Phonétique (Voyelles, Consonnes), Morphologie, Syntaxe, Textes, Glossaire: no accent section; the only 'accent' token is a quotation of Kowalski defining schwa in 'syllabes non accentuées' (p. 232). Silent on placement. Source: https://real-j.mtak.hu/3453/.

sources.citation: Hazai, György. 1959. Les dialectes turcs du Rhodope. Acta Orientalia Academiae Scientiarum Hungaricae 9: 205-229.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Phonetics §§1-42 (vowels, consonants, sandhi); §41 'Accent emphatique' (p. 221) is only a list of forms with emphatic accent; no statement of word-stress placement. Extracted from the REAL-J whole-volume scan (https://real-j.mtak.hu/3465/).

sources.citation: Kakuk, Suzanne. 1958. Le dialecte turc de Kazanlyk I-II. Acta Orientalia Academiae Scientiarum Hungaricae 8: 168-187, 241-311.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Only §6 (p. 170), on loss of intervocalic g: 'l'accent tombe sur la voyelle plus ouverte (aà, à'a, eä')' — accent within a contracted vowel pair; no word-stress rule anywhere in the volume (whole-volume text a full-text search for stress/accent gave this single hit). Source: https://real-j.mtak.hu/3464/.
